findings.summary: xtask/shard-timings.txt is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The plan misses the existing code that enforces the instance split, and records a weaker snapshot test as the mechanism
findings.evidence: I read the code. crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:112-151: `StudyCapability::admit` refuses any change outside one studies/<id>/ directory (rules `study-outside-directory` and `study-one-directory`), and lib.rs:231-314 tests it. rules.rs:1497-1507 (`Loaded::read`) already requires pin.json, claims, rationales, model, findings and validation in each instance. rules.rs:1613-1632 (`conventions`) checks that pin.json's study_id equals the directory name. rules.rs:1841 (`every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates`) runs this over every studies/<id>/. Decision 1 rejects a runtime check as out of scope, but one already exists. The plan's `instance_problems` only re-checks that pin.json exists, which is weaker. Its mechanism text names only the new test file. Fix: Name the real mechanisms in the OLY-B-S1-02 mechanism text: `StudyCapability::admit` in crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs (instance work stays in one studies/<id>/) and the per-instance conventions check in rules.rs. Keep the new athena-core test as the spec-level check, and say in its doc comment that it complements them. Drop the duplicate pin-exists check or make it defer to the conventions test. If the measure should cover them, name their commands too (`cargo test -p athena-cap-study`). athena-core cannot depend on cap-study (crate reach), so cite them; do not call them from the new test.

findings.summary: Matching instance ids as bare substrings will give false positives on the instances the requirement expects next
findings.evidence: `capability_problems` flags any capability file whose text contains an instance id as a substring. The requirement says 'each later instance is studied', and the reading names Athena and Hermes as the next ones. A study with the id `athena` would match `athena_core`, `athena-cap-study` and the word 'Athena' in every cap-study source. A short id such as `model`, `rules` or `pin` would match ordinary words. The plan's risk note calls such hits 'the behaviour wanted'. That holds only for long ids like `firstmate-work-handling`. Today the check passes only because there is one long id; my grep for firstmate|hermes in crates/athena-cap-study found no hits. Fix: Match a specific instance reference, not a substring: the path `studies/<id>` and the id as a whole quoted literal (`"<id>"`). Add negative-case tests with an id like `athena` against a real cap-study source: it must pass when the text only says `athena_core`, and fail on `studies/athena/` or the literal "athena".

findings.summary: The no-nested-directory rule refuses a layout the study capability accepts
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:267 asserts that `admitted(&["studies/a/sub/dir/x.json"])` is empty, so a study job may write nested files. The new test would then fail `cargo test` on a tree that a legitimate study job produced. The json/md-only rule has the same problem: admit places no limit on file types. Fix: Either drop the nested-directory and extension rules and keep only 'no code files (.rs, .sh, etc.) under studies/', or tighten `admit` to match. Tightening admit changes the capability's runtime behaviour, which is out of scope, so dropping the rules is the right choice. State in the test which rules it shares with admit.

summary: The plan fits the accepted reading and one producer run. The files and functions it names exist (I read learnings_recorded.rs, hestia.rs parse_spec/measure_problem/spec_gaps at 1172/1219/1291, and the OLY-B-S1-02 table at spec.toml:2928-2934). Its `status: not shown` measure passes measure_problem, and adding the line to xtask/shard-timings.txt is correct: ci_shards.rs:411-421 compares the file against every workspace test unit, so a new test without a line fails `cargo test`. The dependents list matches the readers I found. But the design has three soundness problems. First, it misses the code that already enforces this split. The study capability's `admit` (crates/athena-cap-study/src/lib.rs:112-151) refuses any study-job change outside one studies/<id>/ directory. A cap-study test (rules.rs:1613-1670, 1841) already requires pin.json and other records in every studies/<id>/ and checks that the pin's study_id matches the directory name. The plan instead records a weaker snapshot test of today's tree as the mechanism and re-implements the pin check. Second, its check for instance names in capability files is a bare substring match. It would give false positives on the next instances the requirement expects, such as a study with the id `athena`. Third, its no-nested-directory rule refuses a layout the capability's own admission accepts.
